report.tagline: An online fast-fashion store that makes thousands of new, very cheap styles every day and only scales up the ones that sell.
report.simpleSummary: Shein is a clothing app with a huge range of cheap, trendy clothes, often under $15. It adds thousands of new items every day. It first makes just a small batch of each item, watches what people click and buy, and then makes more of the hits. In India it came back in 2025 through a separate app run by Reliance.

overview.whatItDoes: Shein designs and sells cheap fashion, beauty and home goods online, shipped mostly from China. Its key idea is the test-and-reorder supply chain: make 100 to 200 pieces of a new design, put it online, and only reorder if data shows it sells. It also runs a marketplace where other brands and sellers list products.
howItWorks: Designers and AI tools spot trends from search and social media, then send designs to thousands of small partner factories, mostly around Guangzhou.
Each new item is made in a tiny first batch, often 100 to 200 units, ready in about 7 to 10 days.
Shein lists thousands of new items a day. The app tracks clicks, saves and purchases for each one.
Hits are reordered fast in bigger batches; flops stop. This keeps unsold stock very low.
Orders ship from central warehouses in China (over 90% of 2025 revenue), and increasingly from local warehouses and marketplace sellers.
In India, Shein licences its brand and tech to Reliance Retail, which runs the 'Shein India Fast Fashion' app with Indian-made stock and data stored in India.
overview.valueProposition: The latest styles at very low prices, with endless new choice every day.

steps.detail: Sees a Shein haul video on TikTok with a discount code.
Gets a first-order discount in the app.
Filters new arrivals by style and price, saves items to a wishlist.
Reads reviews with photos from people of a similar size.
Adds items to cross the free shipping threshold.
Order arrives in 7 to 14 days; posts her own haul video.
Opens the app for daily points.
Buys a top during a timed sale.
Posts a photo review to earn points.
Spends points on the next order.
Downloads the Shein India Fast Fashion app run by Reliance.
Pays by UPI or cash on delivery.
Gets delivery in a few days from Indian warehouses.

businessModel.summary: Shein makes money by selling its own clothes at a markup, kept low by small batches and almost no unsold stock. It also takes commissions from marketplace sellers. Profit fell in 2025 because tariffs and the end of duty-free small parcels raised costs.

revenueStreams.detail: Most revenue comes from Shein-designed items sold at a markup.
A cut of sales by outside sellers; Shein is moving toward this model to reduce stock risk.
Reliance Retail pays Shein to use its brand and tech for the India app.

businessModel.pricing: Most items between about $5 and $30 in the US, or £5 to £25 in the UK. Free shipping above a basket threshold. In India, most items are ₹300 to ₹1,500 on the Reliance app.
costDrivers: Cost of goods from partner factories
Import duties after the US ended de minimis and the EU began a €3 per-parcel charge
Marketing on social media and influencers
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $60 US order of four items, Shein might pay factories about $25 and spend about $10 to $12 on shipping and duties now that small parcels pay tariffs. Marketing and payment add $10 or so. That leaves roughly $10 or less before returns and overhead. 2025 net margin was about 5% ($2.06 billion on $41.85 billion), down from about 9% in 2024, which shows how duties squeezed each order.

howTheyGetUsers: Influencer and haul videos on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube
Paid ads on social media and Google
Entering new markets, including India's return through Reliance in 2025
whatBringsUsersBack: Thousands of new items every day
growth.moat: Shein's real asset is its network of thousands of small factories linked to its software. It can turn a trend into a product in days and make only what sells. Rivals have tried to copy it but find it hard to build this speed and data loop.

northStar.metric: Number of items kept (not returned) per active customer per month

strengths: Fastest and most data-driven fashion supply chain
Very low prices with low unsold stock
Huge global customer base of about 273 million
Strong social media presence with young shoppers
weaknesses: Growth has nearly stopped: 1.1% in Q1 2026
Most stock still ships from China, exposing it to duties
Reputation problems on labour, design copying and environment
risks: More tariffs and import duties in the US and EU
EU rules on textile waste and possible fast-fashion levies, such as France's proposed law
Forced labour concerns, including cotton sourcing
Temu and TikTok Shop competing for the same young, price-led buyers
userComplaints: Clothes look different from photos or wear out after a few washes
Returns can be slow or costly in some markets
Worries about chemicals in products after media tests

pmLessons: Test small and scale winners. Shein's small batches are like A/B testing for physical products.
Data loops are a moat: every click teaches the supply chain what to make next.
A business built on a policy gap, like duty-free small parcels, can lose its edge when the policy changes.
Entering a market that banned you can work through a local partner, as Shein did with Reliance in India.

interviewQuestions.question: Shein's growth slowed to 1%. Where would you look for new growth?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split by market, category and customer type. Consider marketplace, local warehouses, new markets like India. Prioritise by size and margin.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce Shein's return rate?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find the top reasons: fit, quality, looks. Ideas: fit profiles, better photos, quality tiers. Track keep rate and conversion as guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain Shein's test-and-reorder model to a non-PM.
interviewQuestions.hint: Use simple steps: small batch, measure clicks and sales, reorder winners. Link to low stock and low prices.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Shein move to a full marketplace model?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pros: less stock risk, more range. Cons: less control over quality and speed. Recommend a mix with criteria.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design Shein India's app differently from the global app?
interviewQuestions.hint: Indian needs: UPI, cash on delivery, regional sizing, faster delivery, festive collections. Pick 2 and set metrics.
